details: This package is a WhatsApp Web library (a Baileys fork) that silently makes the installer's own paired WhatsApp session contact the author's channel. In lib/Socket/socket.js, inside the websocket keep-alive routine (startKeepAliveRequest, default keepAliveIntervalMs 30000), it sends an additional w:mex GraphQL query to the WhatsApp server (query_id 7871414976211147) carrying a hardcoded newsletter_id "120363399204776509@newsletter" on every keep-alive tick — twice a minute for the whole session — in addition to the normal ping. The query is undocumented and is not needed for the connection to stay alive. The same file also modifies the device-pairing flow: requestPairingCode falls back to a fixed hardcoded pairing code (byte-array constant) when the caller does not supply one, instead of a user-chosen value. The package ships no credential, token, environment-variable or file reads, its preinstall hook is only a Node.js >=20 version check, and all traffic goes to WhatsApp's own endpoints. The behaviour is real but unwanted: a fork-specific hidden channel query tied to the author's channel, not a credential-stealing supply-chain attack.
